claim: SealedRejectDie's sentence for a role that is not known (REJECT_ROLE_UNKNOWN), and the goals desk's and the export shelf's read-only reasons for the same state, no longer say the role has not been read yet or is not known yet, or that it will clear, or to reload. Each is shown when useAuth().activeRole is null (SealedRejectDie: roleUnknown = activeRole === null || activeRole === undefined, which selects REJECT_ROLE_UNKNOWN for the legacy-reject-role-note; useGoalsDesk: activeRole === null; useReportExports: activeRole == null). activeRole is null in more than one state, including before the first /auth/me/role read returns, after a failed read, and when that read finds no role for this person here; /auth/me/role reads only the user_restaurant_access row with is_active = true (auth.service.ts getUserRoleAtRestaurant), while the gateway's assertCanManageRestaurant reads the legacy users row when the access read gives no role (organizations.service.ts lookupRestaurantRole). AuthContext asks about the page's active house, which can differ from the stored token's house, and JwtAuthGuard refuses a role read that names any house but the token's: 403 from the tenant check (assertTenantMatch) once the checks on the token itself pass (the blacklist, then the JWT strategy, which calls validateJwtPayload), or 401 or 503 when one of those fails first; a refusal that reaches the role read is recorded as a failed read. For the token's house, a token naming a house where the person holds no active access row is refused before that route answers (validateJwtPayload, 401 HOUSE_ACCESS_ENDED, and a 503 when that row cannot be read), so the states the code allows in which a read finds no role include an active row whose role is NULL (the column is nullable and the user_restaurant_access_role_known CHECK lets NULL through; production held no NULL role on 2026-09-02, per that migration's header) and a failure of the route's own read, which getUserRoleAtRestaurant answers as no role; for a NULL role the cancel gate's check reads the legacy users row instead, so a member whose users row names this house with the role manager or owner passes that check while activeRole is null. Each sentence now says the role is not confirmed here and names who to ask, with no promise that it clears. REJECT_NEEDS_A_MANAGER now says this page has the person as staff, since, when a read is made, activeRole keeps its old value until that read returns, including after a house switch (with no user, no token or no valid house it is set to null at once). The verify pins the three sentences, the staff sentence's new clause, SealedRejectDie's wiring of roleUnknown to REJECT_ROLE_UNKNOWN in both the role note and the onChallenge fallback, its role-note render, and the null-state list in each of two places, checked separately: the header's rule 4 and REJECT_ROLE_UNKNOWN's docblock. It requires the titles of the three [REVERT-FAILS] tests (each of those tests fails against the sources at 4bd11a00e). It fails if 'clear in a moment', 'Your role at this restaurant has not been read' or 'Your role at this restaurant is not known yet' appears in any .ts, .tsx, .js or .jsx file under apps/web/src or apps/mobile/src, read after two steps: every run of whitespace, line breaks included, becomes one space; then every sequence of a quote mark (single, double or backtick), an optional space, a plus sign, an optional space and another quote mark is removed. That joins adjacent single-quoted, double-quoted and substitution-free template literals, in any mix and across line breaks. It does not catch the phrase written with an escape sequence or an HTML entity in place of a character, split by a template substitution or a comment, or assembled any other way (a variable, an array, a join call). It requires that walk to read more than 500 files. A missing file fails the verify (exit 1). It is static text matching: it does not render the pages or run the tests.
